newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ASM Litho saw market share rise in 1996.
newsitem.headline: ASM Litho saw market share rise in 1996.

text.p: Dutch semiconductor equipment maker ASM Lithography NV said on Thursday it gained market share in 1996, one of the reasons for its earlier announced 66 percent rise in net profit for the year.

Presenting the climb in net profit to 218 million guilders, ASML chief executive Willem Maris told a news conference that the company increased market share to an estimated 19 percent in 1996, up from 17 percent in 1995.
"Our competitive edge is that we can supply a lower cost per chip because we have more output per machine per hour than our competitors," he said in an interview after the news conference.

"We've won market share," Maris told reporters. "Our strategic target is one third of the market and second position (up from a current third) in the market place," he said, but declining to give a timeframe.

He told journalists Nikon, market leader in ASML's sector, saw market share dip to an estimated 45 percent in 1996, from 49 percent in 1995. Second in the market, Canon, had an estimated 26 percent in 1996, against 28 percent in 1995.
Finance director Gerard Verdonschot said profits were boosted by higher sales as well as an improvement in product mix, with average selling prices rising about 25 percent.

He said this was achieved through increased sales of more sophisticated machines, with the average selling price in 1996 rising to 6.10 million guilders per machine, from 4.87 million in 1995, which was up modestly from 4.69 million in 1994.
Maris told reporters ASML would continue to focus its efforts on developing new technology and products as well as reducing costs.
He said the company was targeting average capacity of around 350 machines by mid-1997, up from an average of 250 in 1996, adding more personnel would need to be trained to meet this.

ASML makes "wafer steppers", photolithography projection systems which are essential in making modern semiconductors. The company said it sold 205 wafer steppers in 1996, up from 177 in the previous year.
Philips Electronics said earlier on Thursday it planned to cut its 35 percent stake in ASML to 24 percent via an international offering.
